we pray to answer god who has spoken to us first. we thank you lord for your word. today you let me see that just like those people that approached you, sometimes i also come to you to ask you for my petty things and to try to make you an accomplice of my pettiness. i beg for your help, so that i may be able to change and improve all the time, come closer to you through my prayers and so that i may always approach you to give you praise and worship you. lord, i am now aware of my reflection in the mirror of your word, where i can see my own life…that many times i put my eyes and my heart in mundane things. i am aware of the fact that i carry my life as a reflection of your own image, because i was created in your image and likeness lord. i want to ask for your forgiveness for all the times that i have given my time and my things to worldly things and allowed to be confused by the lies of the world. i want to rebuild my life and my dedication to you god. today, i recognize that you are the only god and that only to you i owe obedience, submission and adoration. 18 october 2026 world mission sunday from the question posed to him by the pharisees, jesus draws a more radical and vital question for each of us, a que stion we can ask ourselves: to whom do i belong? to family, to the city, to friends, to work, to politics, to the state? yes, of course. but first and foremost – jesus reminds us – you belong to go d. this is the fundamental belonging. it is he who has given you all that you are and have. and therefore, day by day, we can and must live our life in recognition of this fundamen tal belonging and in heartfelt gratitude toward our fath er, who creates each one of us individually, unrepeatable, always according to the image of his beloved son, jesus. it is a wondrous mystery. christians are called to commit themselves concretely in the human and social spheres without comparing ‘god’ and ‘caesar;’ comparing god and caesar would be a fundamentalist approach. christians are called to commit themselves concretely in earthly realities but illum inating them with the light that comes from god. the primary entrustment to god and hope in him do not imply an escape from reality, but rather the diligent rende ring to god that which belongs to him. this is why a believer looks to the future reality, that of god, so as to live earthly life to the fullest, and to meet its challenges with courage. may the virgin mary help us to always live in confor mity with the image of god that we bear within us, inside, also offering our contribution to the building of the ear thly city. pope francis greencastle centre - gwyneth & sarahs art camp tues 27th oct 10am-1pm €30 call/text/whats app

gospel reflection (matthew 22:15-21) in todayʼs gospel, religious leaders try to trap jesus with a question about paying taxes to caesar. pointing to the coinʼs image and inscriptio n, he teaches us to fulfil our earthly responsibilities while giving our deepest alle giance to god. jesus reminds us that not every question deserves a fight. what mat ters is whether our choices reflect goodness, truth, and love, drawing us close r to god, strengthening our character, and blessing others. a life we ll lived is measured not by arguments won, but by faithfulness to godʼs will. the coin carried caesarʼs image, reminding us to respect leg itimate laws, perform our duties honestly, support our families, and contribute p ositively to society. faith does not excuse us from responsible citizenship; it inspires us to fulfil our duties with sincerity and fairness. the coin bore caesarʼs image, our lives are called to reflect godʼs goodness. though we cannot do so perfectly every day, we can choose to grow: let our words encourage, our hands help, and o ur hearts forgive. we may give money to the world, time to our responsibilities, and attention to our ambitions, but we must give god what belongs to him: our love, worship, gratitude, trust, and obedience. our relationship with god remains the foundation of a meaningful life. clonleigh (strabane pastoral area)
